answer: A cross-beacon thread-uniqueness rule keeps the wharf honest: each epoch a random beacon signs every active identity's attestation, and the registry stores one signed thread per beacon per identity. When two identities present threads from the same beacon, the collision is proof of shared infrastructure, and both bonds burn — 14,000 POA per fake, while a genuine operator keeps one thread per beacon and passes free. An island of fifty clones therefore torches 700,000 POA unless each fake earns its own beacon signature, a cost no epoch reward repays.
